title: Reading Drill — A test of rotating library exhibitions — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: A test of rotating library exhibitions — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The exhibition librarian had been asked to investigate regular visitors missing exhibits between visits in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on exhibits seen by returning visitors, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used visitor questionnaires at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because changes in opening hours might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a public changeover calendar. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
